pre.speaker: narrator
pre.text: Daxing Hill, Youzhou. The Yellow Turbans under Cheng Yuanzhi sit on the high ground, and between their camp and the road lies a wide field of ripe millet, dry as paper.

pre.speaker: zou-jing
pre.text: Their host is larger than mine, and my levies have never seen a real fight. Give me one good reason not to wait for the imperial army.

pre.speaker: liu-bei
pre.text: The wind is at our backs, sir, and the millet has not seen rain in a month. If the rebels cross it, they cross it on fire.

pre.speaker: jian-yong
pre.text: A spark, a breeze and some patience. I will do the rest, though I would prefer not to be asked to prove it twice.

pre.speaker: zhang-fei
pre.text: Fire? I thought we were going to hit them.

pre.speaker: guan-yu
pre.text: We shall hit them. Fire first, steel after.

pre.speaker: zou-jing
pre.text: Then hold the line at the village and wait for the smoke. If this goes wrong, Liu Bei, I will remember whose idea it was.

post.speaker: narrator
post.text: Cheng Yuanzhi's banner goes down on the hill, and the rebel host breaks and scatters across the blackened millet.

post.speaker: zhang-fei
post.text: Did you see that? Two of them with one swing. My hands are still shaking. Don't tell anyone.

post.speaker: guan-yu
post.text: It is normal. It passes. Do not wait for it to pass before the next one.

post.speaker: liu-bei
post.text: Most of them were farmers a month ago. I want the dead counted, ours and theirs, and I want it written down that we counted.

post.speaker: jian-yong
post.text: I would like to stay with the company, if you can use an unpaid strategist who burns things.

post.speaker: liu-bei
post.text: Gladly, old friend. We have the beginning of an army, and it needs someone who can think.

post.speaker: zou-jing
post.text: Youzhou will not forget today. But a rider has come from Qingzhou, and its governor writes that he cannot hold the walls much longer.
